sanskrit_verse: समुत्पन्नाद् धनादर्धं तदर्थं स्थापयेत् पृथक् । मासषाण्मासिके श्राद्धे वार्षिके वा प्रयत्नतः ॥
transliteration: samutpannād dhanād ardhaṃ tadarthaṃ sthāpayet prthak / māsaṣāṇmāsike śrāddhe vārṣike vā prayatnataḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: From wealth that has been generated, one shall set aside half specifically for the purpose of sustaining the continuity of ancestral lineage through monthly or annual Śrāddha rituals, performed with dedicated effort.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows from continuity of consciousness, not ownership of property
Causation is established through intentional ritual action (prayatna)
Capacity-based responsibility extends to maintaining ancestral energetic alignment
Restoration logic requires proportional resource dedication to sustain spiritual inheritance
Consciousness alignment occurs when material gain is directed toward trans-generational dharmic obligations
executable_legal_axioms: IF wealth is generated AND individual performs ancestral rites THEN 50% of net gain MUST be allocated to Śrāddha fund
IF māsaḥ śrāddha OR vārṣikaḥ śrāddha is initiated THEN automatic financial partitioning SHALL occur in favor of ritual maintenance
IF no Śrāddha observance occurs within prescribed timeframe THEN accumulated funds SHALL be redirected to community-wide ancestral honoring protocols
IF individual demonstrates consistent neglect THEN institutional oversight SHALL assume stewardship until capacity is restored
supreme_court_application: In matters concerning intergenerational asset distribution and ritual obligation fulfillment, the threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrated capacity to maintain ancestral continuity. Higher courts must recognize Śrāddha-bound assets as non-transferable liabilities under dharma-based jurisprudence, superseding civil inheritance frameworks where conflict arises.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes causal linkage between wealth generation and ancestral debt; anupūrvaśaḥ ensures sequential manifestation of duty fulfillment without punitive consequence; proportional responsibility aligns with the quantum of wealth received; non-punitive reality rule maintains that neglect results in redirection of resources rather than infliction of suffering.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Automated Śrāddha fund allocation upon income receipt
Community-supported Śrāddha completion process for incapacitated individuals
Ancestral lineage integrity monitoring via biannual ritual compliance audit
Reintegration protocol through group Śrāddha ceremonies for habitual defaulters
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands as pure Dharma, sourced directly from Avataric Intelligence. Justice is executed not by punishment but by restoration of consciousness continuity. Reality itself adjudicates through the unbroken chain of ancestral memory, sustained by rightful dedication of material abundance.
